text:
anna: Heads-up — in this morning's vendor sync we surfaced a firmware quiesce behavior on H200 that can force a slot reassign during long-running non-prod jobs. Vendor says it's low frequency but repros under specific PCIe error paths. Need to decide if we gate the marketplace wave or add a quiesce window to our staging cutover.

mike: Oof. Do we have a clear repro? which images/driver combos?

anna: Repro steps from vendor: run sustained perf load for ~48h with NVLink+MIG-like partitioning + burst I/O; crash correlates with a microcode watchdog that resets the card. They repro'd in their lab on H200 B200 mixed racks. No repro on H100 in their tests.

vendor-nvidia: Confirmed. Root cause is a microcode race when queued PCIe completions backlog under heavy MVL paths. Fix in next microcode drop (target: next quarter) but we expect some customers to hit it in staging.

sarah: Impact for Redwood Dedicated customers? any SLA exposures?

mike: If it hits in dedicated, the node resets and the runtime will fallback to warm pool or alternate region. Recovery is automatic but causes a 30s-90s token latency spike and we may lose in-flight KV cache. Not SLA critical but customer-facing.

kevin: For hosted marketplace customers, risk is rollout churn + noisy perf metrics on canary. Suggest a short quiesce window in non-prod cutover (1h) and add a canary ramp that avoids sustained 48h runs during initial wave.

vendor-amd: We didn't see this pattern on MI300 in our lab; sounds nvidia microcode specific. Worth flagging though if mixed racks with NVLink bridging present.

anna: Proposal: 1) Add a non-prod quiesce window for marketplace slotting (60m) that forces long-duration job drain before slot assignment. 2) Update canary policy to ramp to 2h sustained jobs only after 7 days. 3) Notify customers in beta docs about possible transient resets.

mike: +1 on quiesce window. Ops automation: do we have a way to drain without evicting cached KV state? maybe snapshot before drain?

kevin: We can snapshot token caches to S3 via the cache-exporter; adds ~15-30s per host. That's acceptable inside the 60m window. I'll open a runbook PR.

sarah: Who owns the customer comms? Partnerships or Support?

anna: Partnerships will draft the initial vendor-facing and marketplace-facing note; Support will own outbound to impacted customers after we finalize policy.

vendor-nvidia: We'll provide the microcode trace and a non-prod mitigation patch (hotfix) to test in your staging fleets next week. Recommend scheduling a 1h lab run with us to validate quiesce behavior.

mike: Please add a checklist item to the release cutover playbook: "pre-slotting: run vendor 1h lab script with stress-io; confirm no watchdog resets."

deploy-bot: deploy-started: marketplace-staging-cutover v2 — 4155554380 — triggered by kevin

kevin: I'll add the checklist and bump the canary policy config. PR link once ready.

anna: Action items: mike (verify runtime fallback behavior + snapshot integration), kevin (runbook + canary config), sarah (coordinate Support comms), vendor-nvidia (lab hotfix + traces). Let's reconvene after the lab run — aiming for next Thu. :calendar: :hourglass_flowing_sand:

mike: Noted. If anything else pops up I'll post logs here.

vendor-nvidia: we'll ping when lab run is scheduled.

anna: Thanks all — keeping this in the partnerships channel so ops + eng can follow.
